items.title: Senator questions No Surprises Act arbitration process as costs skyrocket - benefitspro.com
items.reason: This item directly addresses No Surprises Act enforcement and the Independent Dispute Resolution process, specifically questioning its implementation as costs increase, which is a material development affecting how the law operates.
items.summary: A U.S. Senator has raised concerns about the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) arbitration process as administrative costs have escalated significantly. The article indicates that operational expenses for the IDR system—which resolves disputes between insurers and providers over out-of-network payment rates—have grown to levels that warrant legislative scrutiny. This development affects healthcare revenue-cycle operations by potentially signaling regulatory pressure to reform or restructure the IDR process, which directly impacts how providers and plans resolve payment disputes and manage balance-billing compliance under the federal No Surprises Act.
